summary: Added the last named item of the open gap: a liveness witness in the sweep. After each event's invariant checks the harness now asks whether any node still holds a committed-but-unapplied configuration change and, if so, whether any node is promotable; when unapplied changes are present and nothing can campaign it counts a stalled state, and invariant_sweep_summary reports stalled_states (the two conditions come from the target's own hasUnappliedConfChanges and promotable predicates, so the witness measures the state the campaign guard reacts to rather than a reimplementation). The sweep otherwise keeps the event set built up over the last turns: four real state machines with node 4 starting outside the configuration, single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals on node 4 half of the time with JointImplicit so joint configurations are entered and left through the target's AutoLeave path, committed conf changes applied through applyConfChange, and restarts that rebuild a node from its persisted hard state and applied ConfState. Draft-side this revision reports seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=466, ordinary proposals=452, conf_change_proposals=249, restarts=471, stalled_states=0, violations=0 - so in this event set the guard never left the configuration without a voter able to campaign while a change was pending - and a fresh isolated execution of these bytes is requested, with the changed reported fields as the revision reason. Stated honestly in the request: a zero count over a fixed event set bounds nothing beyond it, and if the receipt reports a non-zero count the summary alone would not carry the decisive operands, so a follow-up would have to emit seed, step and node states per occurrence.
